title: Suki and Pip's Flag Adventure
markdown:
Suki was a super-duper fluffy snow leopard cub, a little white cloud that had landed right on the snow. Big bright blue eyes that twinkled like little stars. The softest paws you ever did see, like little fuzzy slippers. Her best friend was Pip, a puffling, a tiny round bird with a tummy that puffed out like a little balloon and feet the colour of a super juicy orange. When Pip chirped, it sounded like a tiny happy bell. Chirp-chirp-ring.

They lived near a pond. Not a big splashy grumpy ocean pond. A sparkly happy giggly pond, the kind where dragonflies do loop-de-loops and sometimes splash each other just for fun. Their cozy home sat on one sunny side. Across all that shimmering dancing water was Duck Island. The ducks were having a very important party. They needed a flag. A tiny teeny fluttery flag to wave in the breeze.

“Pip,” Suki said. Her fluffy white tail gave a little excited wiggle, making her whole body jiggle. “We have to get this flag to the ducks. It’s super important.”

Pip bounced on his bright orange feet, thump-thump on the grass. “Chirp. Yes. A flag delivery adventure. Oh, I love flag deliveries.”

They did not use a giant fancy ship. They used a marvelous cardboard boat. It made a gentle wobble-wobble-splash when Suki, with a big shove of her soft paws, nudged it into the water. Pip hopped right in and sat on top of the tiny flag so it would not blow away. Red and white, the colour of a yummy strawberry and fluffy clouds, ready to flutter.

“Ready, Pip?” Suki gave a little gentle push against the side. Ripples around her.

“Ready as I’ll ever be.” Pip held the flag up with his beak, making sure it caught the breeze.

Off they went. A gentle happy breeze puffed the cardboard boat across the sparkling water. Suki paddled alongside, big paws making gentle strokes. The shore they started from grew smaller. The sun was warm and bright. The water sparkled like a million tiny diamonds. Pip hummed a happy little tune. La la la, flag for the ducks.

Then a tricky moment. The lily pads, those big round green floating leaves, were a little too far apart for Pip to hop from one to the next. They looked like stepping stones for tiny fairies, but the gaps were a bit too big for puffling hops.

Pip looked at the gaps. He wiggled his bright orange feet nervously. “Chirp?” which in puffling-language meant, this looks like a hop-skip-and-a-jump too far.

Suki looked too. She wiggled her soft cloud-like paws. “Don’t you worry your little orange feet, Pip. I have a super-duper idea.”

She swam closer to the biggest lily pad, the one right next to their boat. Then, with a gentle stretch of her long body and a soft pounce, she landed right on it. Her paws were so soft and light they did not even make the lily pad sink. It just bobbed a little. She stretched again and gently nudged the next lily pad closer. Boop. It moved. Then the next. Boop. A perfect little path for Pip.

“Your turn, Pip. Follow the bouncy green leaves.”

Pip took a deep breath. He held the red and white flag up high like a tiny banner. Boing. He landed safely on the first lily pad. Boing, boing, boing. Suki nudged the pads a tiny bit closer as he went, always a safe easy hop. A floating bridge made of leaves. Pip hopped from one safe green leaf to the next, his little bell-like chirp getting louder.

“We made it. We made it to Duck Island.” His final happy hop onto the sunny soft grass.

And there they were. The ducks, quacking a very happy song, waddling in a big joyful circle. When they saw Pip holding the bright flag they quacked a big happy booming thanks. Pip proudly presented the tiny flag to a very big very friendly mama duck. Flutter, flutter in the gentle breeze. It looked absolutely perfect.

“Thank you, Pip. Thank you, Suki.” The mama duck gave them both a happy little nod. “You’ve made our special party extra special.”

The ducks brought out a huge bowl of the juiciest reddest berries. Suki and Pip sat down with all the happy ducks, nibbling. The sun felt warm on fur and feathers. Happy quacking filled the air. They had sailed the cardboard boat, helped each other across the lily pads, and made the party work.

Suki did not announce that the smallest adventures were the biggest. She only licked berry juice from a paw, watched the red-and-white flag catch the breeze over Duck Island, and let Pip hum his little tune all the way through, twice.
